facts.text: James Joyce lived at the hotel's address.

facts.text: In 1920 James Joyce took up residence there with his wife and two children to finish the manuscript for Ulysses.
facts.excerpt: In 1920, James Joyce followed suit with his wife and two children to finish the manuscript for Ulysses

facts.text: By 1910 T.S. Eliot took up residence in one of the rooms for a time.
facts.excerpt: By 1910, T.S. Eliot, the first of the great foreign literary talents to settle in the neighborhood to study philosophy at the Sorbonne, took up residence in one of the rooms for a time.

facts.text: The hotel is set within three conjoined buildings, each initially built in the 17th century as noble maisons.

facts.text: The Chevalier Group overhaul was overseen by interior architect Didier Benderli.
facts.excerpt: The Chevalier Group overhaul, overseen by interior architect Didier Benderli, lends a more luxurious touch all while keeping the literary connection alive.

facts.text: Books published by Gallimard fill the lounges, from the library to the fireplace salon, and the guest rooms.
facts.excerpt: Books published by Gallimard, whose headquarters are a short walk away, abound in cozy lounges, from the moody library to the fireplace salon, and in guest rooms

facts.text: Rooms have high ceilings, crown moldings, 70s-style furnishings and parquet floors, each with a slightly different color palette.
facts.excerpt: each with Haussmanian high ceilings, crown moldings, plush 70s-style furnishings, parquet floors, curvaceous angles and decorative pieces (mirrors, pillows, bedspreads, wall lights, and more) and a slightly different color palette

facts.text: The top-floor Joyce Suite has exposed wood beams, two bathrooms and unobstructed views over the rooftops of Paris.
facts.excerpt: the most spectacular of the rooms is the top-floor (aptly-named) Joyce Suite—nearly 753 square feet of space with exposed wood beams, two bathrooms, and unobstructed views over the rooftops of Paris

facts.text: Rooms look out over the district's facades and rooftops.
facts.excerpt: The view of the district's facades and rooftops gives you the confused feeling of owning and belonging to Paris.

facts.text: The Spa des Pres is set in the hotel's vaulted cellars, once home to the Quod Libet cabaret where Leo Ferre began his career.
facts.excerpt: In the 20th century, the vaulted cellars of Pavillon Faubourg Saint-Germain were home to the Quod Libet, a mythical cabaret where Léo Ferré, among others, began his career.

facts.text: The steps leading to the former cabaret are classified as a historical monument.
